Hi Matt / Finovate NetOps —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can move the private deployment (VPC + customer-managed VPN) into a brief performance qualification run: 

Summary of customer SLOs (as discussed)
- Latency: p95 tail target for generation/streaming end-to-end <= 120 ms (interactive experience); p99 <= 300 ms
- Throughput: steady-state throughput target ~500 tokens/sec across the cluster (baseline traffic pattern)
- Concurrency: support 80–120 concurrent inference sessions with 1k token average context, burst to 250 concurrent sessions for 90s
- Streaming: chunked streaming required (server push) with max per-chunk delay < 30 ms

Network / deployment constraints we noted:
- Customer will run Redwood Private in their VPC with a site-to-site VPN to their on-prem gateway (IPSec).
- Egress policy: customer restricts outbound IPs; they will need list of static egress IPs from Redwood to allow through their firewall
- Expected internal RTT budget between on-prem app servers and the VPC endpoint: target <= 40 ms one-way

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Matt / NetOps: please share a traceroute and a short packet-capture (tcpdump) from your app subnet to the planned VPC endpoint during a typical hour. Attach file names/note if you already ran anything.
2) Confirm whether your firewall inspects TLS (TLS interception) — this affects mutual TLS and may add ~10–30 ms.
3) We (Jonas + Grace) will prepare a short perf checklist and a set of synthetic tests for you to run (ping, mtr, iperf3, and an app-level streaming probe).
4) Proposed joint troubleshooting window: Tue 2026-05-04 09:00–11:00 PT — can you confirm availability?

I've attached a "network_runbook_v1.pdf" with the test commands and expected baselines. Also included example vpn_trace_20260503.txt (if you want to paste your traceroute output there).

Thanks — goal is that with these artifacts we can do a 2–3 hour qualification run and validate the SLOs.

Best,

Thanks Neha — great recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Streaming behavior: we expect user-facing transcripts arriving at ~200 tokens per second per session during peak. Does the 500 tokens/sec baseline you listed correspond to aggregate per-cluster or per-VPC? We anticipate bursty traffic across ~4 app servers.
2) Context length: our current average context is ~1k tokens but we are testing 4k for certain flows. Does your streaming SLOs assume 1k or 4k?
3) TLS interception: our security stack sometimes uses TLS inspection for egress to public cloud during audits — would that break mTLS between our VPC endpoints and Redwood?

We can run traceroute/iperf3 tomorrow morning and upload to the drive. NetOps: will start a pcap during a simulated load test.

Looping in the tech checklist from our runtime/infra perspective. Short answers first, then items for NetOps: 

Short answers:
- "500 tokens/sec" = aggregate across the Redwood serving cluster mapped to your deployment (not per-session). We size containers to serve that aggregate with the latency SLOs when the network budget holds.
- Streaming SLOs in Neha's note assumed ~1k token contexts; 4k will increase KV cache pressure and could add ~20–50 ms depending on model/kernel. We'll need to validate with a quantized model profile if you're planning consistent 4k context usage.
- TLS interception will break mutual TLS (mTLS) unless you terminate and re-issue certs inside the VPC; it will also make certificate pinning and client-auth fail. If inspection is mandatory, we need to agree on an allowlist for our Palo Alto/Firewall rules or run in a VPC with controlled egress and an outbound proxy under your control.

NetOps checklist / information we need from you (please provide values if available):
- MTU on the path (customer on-prem NIC -> VPN -> VPC): suggested >= 1500; if lower (e.g., 1400) we need fragmentation behavior tested.
- VPN tunnel type and throughput per tunnel (IPSec/IKEv2, vendor/version) and whether you've enabled ECN/DF handling.
- Expected one-way median RTT from app host to VPC endpoint (past 24h baseline).
- Any active TCP proxies (NGINX/LB) that might alter keepalive or connection pooling; our runtime uses long-lived connections and expects keepalive > 300s.
- Firewall CPU/memory headroom during load (to estimate added packet processing latency).

Recommended tests (commands available in the attached runbook):
- mtr -c 100 --json <vpc-endpoint> (gives hop stats and jitter)
- iperf3 -c <vpc-endpoint> -P 10 -t 60 (udp/tcp tests)
- tcptraceroute / traceroute with ICMP/TCP probes to detect load balancer latency
- app-level streaming probe: small websocket/chunked POST sending 128-byte chunks at target rate and measuring server-side ACK/arrival times

If you can paste a sample traceroute and iperf run to vpn_trace_20260503.txt, we can pre-check and provide a prioritized remediation list.

I can be on the troubleshooting call Tue 09:00–10:30 PT. If you want extended testing (throughput + concurrency), plan for 2 hours.
